newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk union sees way to avert strike,no progress.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk union sees way to avert strike,no progress.

text.p: A union leader at the flagship plant of Russia's troubled Norilsk Nickel metals group said on Monday that there was still time to avert planned strikes but that formal talks with management had got nowhere.

Boris Degtyaryov, deputy chairman of the plant's United Trade Union Committee, said negotiations with management had been fruitless but that the government could save the day with tax relief measures to free up funds for salary and other debts.
"There's still time to take constructive measures to avoid a strike," he said by telephone from Norilsk. "But we have gotten nowhere in our talks with management, and so we are adhering to our plan."
Committee leaders have said that a one-hour warning strike is planned for March 27 -- a day of nationwide labour protests -- and wider action on April 2.
Degtyaryov said managers had not responded to a union proposal to extend the work of a reconciliation commission aimed at resolving a bitter dispute over wage and other arrears.
"They missed the five-day deadline we gave them, which is highly unconstructive," he said.

He said that Alexander Khloponin, the chairman of RAO Norilsky Nickel NKEL.RTS 0#NKEL.RUO, the parent company of the flagship plant, was due to arrive in the Arctic town Norilsk on Wednesday for talks.
Norilsk is one of the world's leading producers of nickel and platinum group metals.
It owes workers at the main plant around 900 billion roubles ($160 million) in wages unpaid over two months.
